body:
## Established (OBSERVED, real browser, against main's deployed SPA)

`Reader.tsx` paints highlights via
`rendition.annotations.highlight(cfi, data, cb, className, styles)` with
`styles = { fill: HILITE_FILL[color], 'fill-opacity': '0.35' }`.

epub.js's own `Highlight` defaults are
`{ fill: "yellow", "fill-opacity": "0.3", "mix-blend-mode": "multiply" }`
(`epubjs/dist/epub.js:9918`). **Passing a `styles` object replaces those defaults rather
than merging**, so the rendered rect computes to `mix-blend-mode: normal`. Confirmed by
reading `getComputedStyle` on the live `.cwng-hl` rect, not inferred:

    { tag: "g", cls: "cwng-hl", fill: "#e6c34a", fillOpacity: "0.35", blend: "normal" }

**Pre-existing on main**, not introduced by the notes/drawer/full-screen work —
`HILITE_FILL`, the `0.35`, and the three theme grounds are identical on `origin/main`.

Highlights **are visible on all three page themes**. Light, sepia and dark each showed
clear separation between highlighted and unhighlighted ground on the same line. There is
no "invisible on dark" bug — that was a hypothesis from static math, and the browser
refuted it.

## NOT established, and why this is filed rather than fixed

Precise text-vs-ground contrast *underneath* a highlight is **unresolved**. Two static
models (straight alpha; multiply) disagreed with each other, and neither reconciled with
the measured pixels — so the rig (modal colour over the highlight group's bounding box,
which spans several line rects plus the gaps between them) is not trustworthy at this
precision. Publishing a number from it would be false confidence.

The cell worth a real check is **sepia**, which the straight-alpha model put at 3.9-4.4:1
for all four colours — under the 4.5:1 AA floor for body text — while light and dark
cleared it. Sepia is also the theme least likely to be checked by hand.

## Suggested next step

Measure with the a11y harness rather than an ad-hoc script: sample a single line rect
away from glyph pixels. `notes/ui-sweep-harness/audit.py` is the right instrument. If
sepia is genuinely sub-AA, the cheap fix is a per-theme `fill-opacity`, not new colours —
the fills are shared with the Kobo/legacy highlight set and should stay aligned.

Also worth deciding deliberately: whether dropping `mix-blend-mode: multiply` was
intended. Multiply keeps text darker than the highlight on light grounds but cannot
lighten, so it is the wrong operator for a dark reading theme; `normal` is arguably
correct here. It simply isn't currently a *decision* — it is a side effect of how the
`styles` argument works, and the next person to add a style will re-encounter it.
title: Reader highlight styling drops epub.js mix-blend-mode; under-highlight contrast unmeasured on sepia
